item.content:encoded:
Worcester: Cancelled (rain), end of season
Remember when Portland’s last game of the season was cancelled due to rain? Oh, that was just last week.
Well, as we’re stuck in a cycle of weekend storms, the last game of the season was cancelled for the WooSox. A factor in this decision was Worcester being eliminated from playoff contention on Saturday night. Still, for the season to end so unceremoniously calls for at least some commemoration, and so I’d like to shout out some names on the roster. I originally intended on going down the line on the website and speculate on future contributions to the team, but, by my estimation, especially since the trade for Adley Rutschman that had a ripple effect through the organization, a good portion of Worcester’s roster are either one-year placeholders until the farm gets replenished with the next couple of drafts or guys that are dealing with significant injuries. So, here’s to the guys that may not be that:
Allan Castro finished the season with 77 RBIs, two behind Bobby Dalbec for the team record since they relocated to Worcester five years ago… and saying that relocation happened six seasons ago is crazy for someone who went to the first home stand under pandemic crowd protocols. Castro really was a constant for the offense amidst a handful of platoon guys cycling through the team and that can’t be understated. He batted doubtful games back into contention and sealed close games away. If I pick a workhorse/general player of the year, it’s him or Braiden Ward, but only because Franklin Arias started the year in Portland.
Speaking of Braiden Ward, I personally was sad to see Brennan Bernardino go this offseason but loved the return from Colorado. And he performed fantastically, particularly near the end of the season. He ended up swiping 61 total bags and ther’s some clamor around a potential call-up to the Sox who, despite being a generally quick team in terms of baserunning, lack a real Dave Roberts-esque “when you see him, you know he’s going to steal” threat. Ward provides that, is defensively versatile, playing second as well as center field, and is pretty reliable with the bat in a pinch.
Franklin Arias is banging on the door and he will definitively be getting the call either in 2027 or Opening Day 2028, depending entirely on the length of the lockout. Either way, though, keeping him off the 40-man roster for now means, even with a lockout, he’ll get valuable time to improve his exceptional swing even more, though not against Major League arms. His totals across Portland and Worcester read like an All-Star caliber player: 28 home runs, .323/.400/.557 slash line, a 14% strikeout rate, and a plus glove in the infield to boot. Arias may or may not live up to his sky high prospect status, but pencil him in to the next iteration of this Red Sox team, whenever that comes.
John Holobetz will also likely be given the call in 2027. He’s still just 24. The 6’3” righty struck out 132 in 119 innings, walked just 36, had a WIP of a hair under 1.25, but even more comforting is he outperformed his Portland numbers in Worcester, signaling quick growth. While it’s sad that Quinn Priester missed 2026 with an injury, he was a world-beater in 2025, and the value of having steady presence in the rotation can’t be understated Depending how he bounces back in 2027, especially with the Brewers emerging as an NL front runner, expect that trade to go down in the history books as a win-win.
Hayden Mullins also put in his best work in 2026, and more specifically, directly before his promotion to Triple-A right before the end of the season. He celebrated his 26th birthday last Monday and so, in his age-25 season, Mullins was exactly what Portland needed in a rotation guy, especially following Anthony Eyannson’s departure. He struck out 132 in 92 innings, walked 49, lacked the longevity that Holobetz and others in the rotation had but did not give up long balls, getting taken yard just seven times all season (and even one of those was in his only Worcester appearance.) The 6’0” lefty will continue his development in 2027 before likely a late season call-up; it’s possible the team explores some multi-inning reliever roles depending on how this development goes.
Of course, too, the team’s former first-round draft pick Mikey Romero and current millionaire Kristian Campbell are still kicking around Wrocester, and the latter wants a redemption arc after a rough 2025. Neither saw any Major League time due to a cluttered roster and a multitude of other reasons, but don’t count either out for a platoon role next year, pending a lengthy lockout. You want guys looking better in September than they did in April, and while Campbell swung somewhat of a hot bat in the spring, I think that notion is true for both of these guys. The same is even true with Jedixson Paez (who saw Major League action, but don’t mention this to him) Blake Wehunt and Gage Ziehl. These are all guys to watch in 2027, provided some trade for a hole on the roster doesn’t call for dealing one of them (I think Campbell is pretty set on this roster given his price tag.) But, depth is a good problem to have.
And so ends my fourth full season providing Minor Lines for Over The Monster. You’ll see me kicking around during the playoff push and the offseason providing input on pieces that can make this 2027 team - and farm - even better than the 2026 version. Thanks so much for reading all season, and Go Sox!

item.content:encoded:
The WooSox roster has a bunch of guys who’ve made some plays for the Major League roster this season. But, as far as the Triple-A club is concerned, few guys (I know, I know, Franklin Arias might be one) have had as many big moments as Allan Castro. This wasn’t the 23-year-old’s strongest season from an OPS standpoint, but the big moments are getting notable. He just had a go-ahead home run the other day and he’s had multiple other walkoffs throughout the season. Yesterday, the WooSox again started a series on the winning side due to his bat, as he hit a 2-out single to score the Manfred runner. And, yes, in the process of all of this, Franklin Arias got himself a knock as did Romy Gonzalez. (Here’s that Castro hit.)
The game in general was a defensive battle. The Durham Bulls (Rays AAA) had the benefit of up-and-down starter Mason Englart dealing on Tuesday night as they couldn’t get on the board until Englart departed after seven. Luckily, Jedixson Paez was just as hot even without some of the strikeout numbers. His only run allowed was via a home run way back on the second at-bat of the game, and the 22-year-old righty recovered wonderfully from that, retiring fifteen consecutive Durham batters. From there, Tanner Houck came in and struck out the side in his rehab appearance, and it is starting to look likely that he sees some innings in a relief capacity as the Red Sox’s magic number dwindles. Osvaldo Berrios and Hobie Harris would then slam the door even in the face of a few more Bulls scoring opportunities; the WooSox had the only opportunity with runners in scoring position of the game. Enter extra innings, and enter Castro’s sealing single. Game over, 2-1.

item.content:encoded:
ARLINGTON, Texas — Among a series of minor injury updates offered by Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy on Tuesday came some finality on one key reliever. Righty Justin Slaten, after further assessment by a renowned orthopedist in the Dallas area, won’t return to the Red Sox this year.
Slaten visited Dr. Keith Meister on Monday’s off day and testing on his injured elbow revealed “degenerative changes in the flexor mass,” according to Tracy. Slaten is set for a platelet-rich plasma (PRP) injection that is all but certain to rule out his return in 2026.
“It’s a big loss,” Tracy said, “at least now, with the finality of knowing we can’t have him back.”
Slaten was placed on the injured list with elbow inflammation in mid-August and dealt with recurring discomfort as he tried to resume throwing. As of the weekend, he was completely shut down from his progression. Now, he will receive the injection and rest in hopes of getting the issue fixed for 2027.
“Probably just means a chronic thing over time, but I’m speculating there,” Tracy said. “I just know that the conservative course of action is PRP, then he’s gonna rehab and go from there. Because of that, it’s probably going to cost him the rest of the season.”
Slaten appeared in 36 games for the Red Sox this year, posting a 4.60 ERA as a mid-relief option ahead of setup man Garrett Whitlock and closer Aroldis Chapman. For the third straight season, injuries were a big part of Slaten’s season. In 2024, he missed about six weeks due to elbow inflammation in July and August. Last season, he was out from June 1 to August 28 with a balky shoulder. This year, he suffered an oblique strain in early April and missed 31 games, then hit the IL again for the final six weeks.
Mead takes step forward
For the first time since having his left wrist broken by a wayward pitch in West Sacramento on July 27, Curtis Mead will do some offensive work in Boston on Wednesday. According to Tracy, Mead — who is out of a cast and has been doing defensive and baserunning drills for weeks — will hit lightly off a tee as he begins his swing progression.
“Mead will begin, tomorrow, introducing tee work,” Tracy said. “Obviously, we’ve talked a lot about the defensive stuff, being able to catch throws and he’s been doing that. Tomorrow, he’ll start doing some tee work with a light bat and then just kinda progress from there.”
With just 12 games left in the regular season, Mead is in a race against the clock to be fully ready for game action, a reality he acknowledged just last week. But it’s still notable that he’s ready to start taking swings in anticipation for potentially returning during the postseason if the Red Sox make a run.
Crochet throws again at Fenway
Left-hander Garrett Crochet took another small step toward a late-season return Tuesday, throwing a two-inning “up-and-down” bullpen (that includes a break simulating a between-inning breather) at Fenway Park. That session came four days after a one-inning high-intensity bullpen on the same mound.
“That went well,” said Tracy. “Everything went well.”
The next step for Crochet might be facing hitters in a live batting practice/simulated game setting but it’s very unlikely he’ll be ready to pitch in a rehab game before Triple-A Worcester’s season ends Sunday. A more likely scenario involves him getting into a simulated game or two and then making a relief appearance late in next week’s final homestand of the year.
“We’ll wait and see on the next steps,” Tracy said. “That was the most volume he’s had, so we’ll see how he feels and go from there.”
Guerrero close to return, Kelly has setback
Right-hander Tyron Guerrero, out since September 1 with shoulder inflammation, is with the Red Sox in Arlington and is expected to be activated before Wednesday’s game. Lefty Raymond Burgos and righty Wyatt Olds are the two leading candidates to be sent down as Guerrero takes a roster spot.
“We’ll see how everything goes with that today,” Tracy said.
The return of Guerrero will give the Red Sox another high-octane option at the end of a bullpen that also includes lefty Erik Miller, Whitlock and Chapman (and won’t have Slaten for the rest of the year).
One reliever who won’t contribute the rest of the way is righty Zack Kelly, who has been out since early July with a stress reaction in the olecranon (bone at the tip of the elbow). Kelly had been throwing live BP sessions in Fort Myers and was close to a rehab outing but had a setback last week and will undergo updated imaging this week.
Rafaela progressing
Center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela (right quad strain) has said his goal is to rejoin the Red Sox for this weekend’s series against the Rays and that is still in play. He’s back in Boston and going through strength tests on his leg while ramping up his running program.
“Started to increase running volume today,” Tracy said. “Nothing new to report there. He’ll continue to do that over the next 2-3 days and we’ll see where he’s at.”
The Red Sox could be careful with Rafaela and welcome him back early next week when the Guardians are at Fenway Park.
Houck, Oviedo on track for rehab outings
Right-hander Tanner Houck is pitching for the WooSox at Polar Park on Tuesday as planned. His outing was planned as a shorter relief outing (he entered in the seventh, following six strong innings for starter Jedixson Paez) and he’s expected to make another appearance over the weekend in a longer stint on the mound.
Right-hander Johan Oviedo is still on track to make a rehab start in Worcester on Thursday.
